 Lance Jenkinson from Newswire 15, Nov • 6m read Star ejected in fiery derby ending as Boomer battle explodes; overtime thriller stuns - NBL Wrap Share Melbourne United superstar Cole Anthony showed the importance of nailing your number one import slot, destroying a South East Melbourne Phoenix team that axed its own high profile import 11 games into the season.
 Anthony lit up John Cain Arena on Saturday night, taking over the Throwdown with a 39-point, seven-rebound, three-assist, three-steal game in a too-close-for-comfort 102-95 victory.
 Watch every NBL game LIVE with ESPN on Kayo Sports |  Get Kayo now > 
 The 26-year-old was in the zone from the outset, unguardable at times as he racked up 27 before half time, the best first half by any player in the league this season.
 Anthony's night ended prematurely, exiting with seven seconds left in the game after picking up an unsportsmanlike foul for flailing his arm at Phoenix guard Nathan Sobey.
 That pair had an enthralling running battle all game.
 After giving up 71 first half points to Illawarra on Wednesday night, Phoenix coughed up 64 to United and coach Josh King had a major headache with his team down 25 at half time.
 Phoenix might have its flaws, which have been exposed in recent games, but giving up is not one of them.
 Sobey had a massive second half to inspire the never-say-die Phoenix.
 "That was maybe one of his best games that I've seen him play in quite some time on both sides of the ball," King said.
 After scoring just two first half points, the veteran engineered a gallant Phoenix fightback, lifting to finish with 23 points, six rebounds, eight assists and four steals.
 "Throwdowns are always fun, they're always great games," Chance said.
 "We've beaten these guys two times in a row.
 "We knew there was going to be a response and credit to South East, even when I thought the game was done and our young guys deserved to be out there, they've been really good in those moments, had a little bit of a slip up tonight.
 "Credit Sobes [Phoenix veteran Nathan Sobey], he makes some big plays down the end there to keep it entertaining.
 "Just happy to get away [with the win]."

 Phoenix kept it interesting late, cutting the deficit to five with 24.1 left on the clock, but United kept them at arm's length, maintaining its dominance over the Melbourne derby.
 United has won all three Throwdowns this season, made it four in a row overall and seven of the past eight.
 Aside from Thursday's hiccup against Adelaide, United is one of the form team's of the competition, moving back into the top three.
 The Jacob Chance-coached team made it five wins in six games, while Phoenix lost a fourth straight to remain stuck on the bottom of the ladder.
 Phoenix must be in a rush to find their import replacement for departed floor general Skylar Mays because it could have been a difference maker against United.
 After producing just 10 points as a team in the first quarter against Adelaide on Thursday night, United was more potent out of the blocks with Anthony eclipsing that on his own with 12 first quarter points.
 United racked up 20 points inside five minutes.
 Phoenix import D'Shawn Schwartz swam hard against the tide with 17 points.
 Schwartz's ability to create separation in the mid-range gave Phoenix a weapon away from the long ball and he had 10 at the half.
 There was the usual physicality of a Throwdown with Sobey giving Anthony an accidental clip behind the ear.
 It did not unsettle Anthony, who carved up Phoenix with his speed and skill.
 "Cole's been recruited for a reason," Chance said.
 "When we put all the pieces together, the guy next to me [Waardenburg], JO [Josh Oduro], CG [Chris Goulding], the list goes on, LT [Luke Travers], it was like, what's this last piece that we need and we felt like we needed the perimeter scoring off the bounce.
 "When you look at last year's two grand final teams, how do you compete with Kendric [Davis] and Bryce [Cotton] in those moments when the game slows down a little bit come playoff time.
 "Hopefully we can get there, but that's his role in this team."
 Powerhouse Sam
 The ever-improving Sam Waardenburg made his presence felt for United.
 The former Cairns Taipan arrived with big wraps on him as a key recruit, but made a slow start to his time with United.
 The 27-year-old is showing his full potential now, carving up Phoenix with 16 points, nine rebounds, two blocks and a game best +21 plus-minus.
 His biggest moment came late when Phoenix were making a push, blocking Phoenix centre Yannis Morin at the rim.
 United finished the half on a 13-0 run to take control of the game.
 Phoenix came out with all guns blazing after half time, going on an 8-0 run, including threes to Jordan Hunter and Sobey, signalling their intent to fight until the bitter end.

 Kristian Doolittle shrugged off a disappointing first half to lead the Perth Wildcats to a 111-100 overtime win over the Illawarra Hawks at RAC Stadium on Saturday night.
 Doolittle added 22 points after half-time, including five in overtime, to guide the Wildcats to a second consecutive win.
 Scores were tied at 92 apiece after regular time, after Makur Maker and Milton Doyle both missed last-seconds shots to get the job done for the Hawks in 40 minutes.
 Tyler Harvey looked to have got the Hawks home, with nine points in the fourth term, all three-pointers, after he had also been quiet early.
 But the Hawks kept sending Doolittle to the line in the run home and he kept knocking down the bonus points.
 Doolittle’s three-pointer with 10 seconds remaining in regular time then ended up tying the game.
 The Hawks were without William Hickey during over-time, who fouled out late in the fourth term. Maker followed him to the bench with five fouls early in extra-time.
 BIG CAT REGROUPED
 Doolittle was unhappy when he drew a personal foul for pushing in a rebound battle late in the second quarter.
 He didn’t like the call and let the referee know about it, also drawing a category one technical foul.
 He sat down with three fouls and only seven points next to his name and Perth looked in trouble.
 The Wildcats had dominated the second term at that stage, winning it 18-8 and leading the game 44-38.
 The Hawks made the most of the Perth star sitting on the bench and went on a 10-6 run for the rest of the quarter.
 The Wildcats held a small two-point lead at half-time, but they could have been much further in front.
 They’d probably have taken it though, considering they had trailed at the main break in each of their previous seven games.
 The time Doolittle spent on the bench was clearly well used.
 BIG-TIME SHOOTING
 Illawarra has got itself back in this season on the back of a high field-goal shooting percentage.
 In recent wins against Perth, Cairns and South East Melbourne Phoenix, they shot at better than 50 per cent.
 Against the Taipans, the Hawks lifted that to an incredible 60 per cent.
 On Saturday, they had 30 points on the board at quarter-time, shot at a ridiculous 70 per cent.
 That included having made five of seven shots from long range.
 Makur Maker already had three three-pointers and 13 points next to his name.
 He managed to add just one in the second term though and the shots for the Hawks refused to drop.
 They shot at just 35 per cent from the field in the second term, adding only 18 points.
 The three-point shooting left them after quarter-time. They trailed Perth 69-66 at three-quarter-time having made just seven of 20 shots from long range.
 STILL TOO BIG
 When Illawarra beat Perth a few weeks ago, an advantage of 15 rebounds played a big part in that result.
 Perth trailed in the rebound battle for most of the game, but ended up winning it 47-44.
 Jo Lual Acuil is still sidelined for Perth and Brandon Knight is still starting on the bench as he makes his way back from injury.
 The Wildcats went with both Cameron Huefner and Alex Higgins-Titsha in their starting line-up.
 And the Hawks took advantage, leading 10-4 in rebounds at quarter-time.
 Sam Froling and Maker each had as many boards as the whole Wildcats team.
 By half-time, Maker and Froling had 15 boards between them, three more than the entire Wildcats team.
 Dylan Windler did most of the heavy lifting, with 11 boards to go with 22 points in a second consecutive double-double performance.
